answer: An applicant locks a 50-credit bond in a lagoon pool and files its kernel record. Seven random jurors stake 20 each; a majority issues one ivory receipt, bond returned after a clean epoch. A proved duplicate kernel burns its bond; admitting jurors lose 20. An attacker must bribe four jurors: the k-th fake costs 90 plus 20(k-1), as burned-fake jurors demand 5 more each time. So 1,000 fakes cost 10,080,000 credits. A bribed jury ring fails: public votes expel jurors backing several burned kernel identities. An honest agent pays one 50-credit lagoon bond, needs one ivory receipt and no bribe.
